subject.title: [Bug]: Hundreds of repeated HTTP requests to 169.254.169.254:80 for the first 10 minutes after the startup

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked Bedrock-local behavior boundary where no-signal memory auto-detection skips IMDS, while explicit Bedrock memory configuration can still use the AWS SDK default chain?
rationale: The issue is a real sandbox/security-noise regression, but the repair changes auth-provider fallback behavior for AWS metadata credentials and needs human ownership of that compatibility boundary.

options.title: Land after credential-mode proof
options.body: Require or run proof for both no-signal IMDS suppression and at least one explicit Bedrock default-chain credential path before closing the issue.

options.title: Accept source-backed proof
options.body: Treat the SDK contract, focused tests, and linked PR proof as sufficient once CI is green, accepting the remaining live-environment risk.

options.title: Revise the fix boundary
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask the PR to preserve more implicit credential probing or document a different explicit opt-in behavior.

recommendation.title: Land after credential-mode proof
recommendation.body: Require or run proof for both no-signal IMDS suppression and at least one explicit Bedrock default-chain credential path before closing the issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The current adapter boundary and prior Bedrock credential-gate history point to steipete as the best routing owner for the compatibility/security choice.
